task: Evaluate and report on a training-free framework for improving fine-grained perception of MLLMs by task-guided cropping/zooming to mitigate fixed-resolution vision encoder information loss for small objects.
explicit_methodological_commitments: zoom local detail while preserving global context
use available demo images in data/demo_imgs
produce methodology, results, validation/comparison plots, and discussion
initial_assumptions: No MLLM inference endpoint is guaranteed in the workspace; if unavailable, use deterministic image-analysis proxies for information retention and crop utility.
Related-work PDFs will be used to refine method names, comparison axes, and interpretation.
related_work_refinements: V*: LLM-guided visual search, target locations, and visual working memory are central named mechanisms to approximate with deterministic question/task-guided ROI selection and a global+local visual memory panel.
Monkey: uniform high-resolution patches provide a comparison baseline against selective task-guided crops.
BLIP-2: frozen image encoders motivate analysis of fixed-resolution information loss.
Chefer et al.: attention/saliency explanations motivate exporting saliency/interest maps for ROI interpretability.
fallback_scope: No actual MLLM weights/API are assumed; analysis quantifies image information retention and crop detail using deterministic computer-vision proxies, and visually audits whether selected crops correspond to plausible task-relevant regions.
